high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Organizational Structure Changes
high.summary: Decree No. 198/2026/NĐ-CP has officially amended the organizational structure of the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV). Key changes include: maintaining 20 departments while renaming the Credit for Economic Sectors Department to Credit Department, and the Forecast, Statistics - Monetary and Financial Stability Department to Forecast and Statistics Department. The decree also clarifies that Transaction Offices and Regional State Banks are administrative organizations equivalent to departments under the SBV. This restructuring reflects the central bank's efforts to streamline operations and improve policy coordination. For FX and bond markets, these organizational changes signal potential improvements in monetary policy implementation and coordination between departments, which could lead to more effective policy transmission mechanisms affecting VND exchange rates and government bond yields.

high.title: Securities Firms' Proprietary Trading Heavily Sells Bank Stock ACB During Market Rally
high.summary: Despite VN-Index gaining 12.54 points (+0.69%) to 1,831.55 points, breaking a 7-session losing streak, proprietary trading desks of securities firms net sold VND 369 billion on HOSE. ACB was the most heavily sold bank stock with VND -82 billion in net selling by proprietary traders, followed by MBB (-49 billion) and VIB (-34 billion). Foreign investors shocked the market with massive net selling of VND 5,760 billion across all exchanges. This heavy institutional selling of banking stocks during a market recovery suggests underlying concerns about the banking sector's fundamentals or profit-taking after recent gains. The divergence between market recovery and institutional bank stock selling warrants close monitoring for potential sector-specific headwinds.

high.title: Foreign Investors Post Explosive Net Selling of Nearly VND 7.2 Trillion in First Week of June
high.summary: Foreign investors unleashed massive selling pressure in the first week of June, with net outflows reaching VND 7.192 trillion across all markets. HOSE bore the brunt with VND 7.342 trillion in net selling, while HNX and UPCoM saw modest net buying. VIC (Vingroup) was the primary target with VND 4.820 trillion in net selling. The selling peaked on Thursday with nearly VND 5.8 trillion, mostly through block trades. This represents one of the largest weekly foreign outflows in recent memory and signals potential concerns about Vietnam's economic outlook, corporate earnings, or global risk-off sentiment. The scale of selling could pressure VND and create headwinds for Vietnamese asset prices, while potentially offering attractive entry points for domestic investors with longer-term horizons.

medium.title: Domestic Investors Pour Hundreds of Trillions into Vietnamese Stocks, Countering Foreign Selling Pressure
medium.summary: Domestic investors have provided strong support to Vietnamese equity markets, with nearly VND 70 trillion in net buying year-to-date 2026 on HOSE. Since 2022, domestic net buying has reached over VND 280 trillion, successfully offsetting persistent foreign selling pressure. Foreign ownership has dropped to a record low of around 12% of market capitalization.

medium.title: Savings Interest Rates as of June 2: Latest Updates from Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank
medium.summary: Big 4 state banks maintain identical online deposit rates: 4.75%/year for 1-3 month terms, 6.6%/year for 6-9 months, and 6.8%/year for 12-18 month terms. Private banks offer varying rates with LPBank leading at 7.1%/year for 18-month deposits.

medium.title: VPBank Employee Offers Nearly 9% Interest Rate Despite Maximum Listed Rate of 6%
medium.summary: VPBank staff are offering preferential rates up to 8.9%/year for 6-9 month deposits above VND 50 billion, significantly higher than published rates. This indicates intensifying competition for large deposits among Vietnamese banks.

medium.title: Gold Prices Fall Sharply by Nearly VND 4 Million per Tael on June 5
medium.summary: SJC gold prices continued declining to VND 149.2-153.2 million per tael, down VND 3.8 million on the buying side and VND 2.8 million on the selling side compared to previous session. The sharp correction reflects global gold price volatility and domestic market adjustments.
